# A kept setting outlives the process. Each run prints the count it mounted
# with and keeps one more, so the second run reads what the first kept: gtk4
# in settings.json under $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/Kept, fyne in the Preferences of the
# app whose ID is "Kept". A run only keeps its values because its own main
# opened the place; a test never does (testdata/settings_kept.txtar).
#
# bubbletea keeps them in the same file as gtk4 (pkg/go/snglsettings' tests)
# and needs a terminal to run.

[toolchain] [!headless] skip 'running it needs the headless compositor go tool verify provides'

env XDG_CONFIG_HOME=$WORK/config

sngl run --lang go --platform gtk4 app.sngl
stdout '^count 0$'
sngl run --lang go --platform gtk4 app.sngl
stdout '^count 1$'

sngl run --lang go --platform fyne app.sngl
stdout '^count 0$'
sngl run --lang go --platform fyne app.sngl
stdout '^count 1$'

-- app.sngl --
import go "sngl:language/go"
import settings "sngl:settings"
import time "sngl:time"
import ui "sngl:ui"

#[go.native("fmt", "fmt.Print")]
func print(s string)

#[go.native("os", "os.Exit")]
func exit(code int)

output(name="Kept") {
    go {
        gtk4
        fyne
    }
}

var count option[int] = null
var ticks = 0

// The first tick reports the count the window mounted with and keeps one
// more; the second, after that write was kept, ends the run.
time.timer(interval=200ms, @tick {
    ticks += 1
    if ticks == 1 {
        var n = count
        if n != null {
            print("count {n}\n")
            count = n + 1
        }
    } else {
        exit(0)
    }
})

ui.window {
    settings.kept(name="count", default=0, :value=count)
    ui.text(value=count != null ? "{count}" : "")
}
-- testrun/run/fyne/go/app.sngl/1 --
sha256:dd29f23c0671ecbe29a0065121ee827e
{
  "stdout": "count 0\n"
}
-- testrun/run/fyne/go/app.sngl/2 --
sha256:dd29f23c0671ecbe29a0065121ee827e
{
  "stdout": "count 1\n"
}
-- testrun/run/gtk4/go/app.sngl/1 --
sha256:5d0bd5036856b2916496c3d8abc9152b
{
  "stdout": "count 0\n"
}
-- testrun/run/gtk4/go/app.sngl/2 --
sha256:5d0bd5036856b2916496c3d8abc9152b
{
  "stdout": "count 1\n"
}
